moat.description: QuickBooks dominates as a system of record for 7M+ SMBs with all five AI-resilient moats rated strong, while TurboTax faces secular margin pressure from free alternatives even as IRS Direct File's death removed the biggest government threat. GenOS agent rollouts (3M customers, 85% return) deepen the proprietary-data flywheel without repairing the weakened bundle thesis after the Mailchimp pullback.
moat.analysisTitle: The Ecosystem Moat — Polarised but Durable
moat.analysisSummary: Intuit's moat profile is **sharply polarised**: all five AI-resilient moats (proprietary data, regulatory lock-in, network effects, transaction embedding, system of record) remain strong, while all five AI-vulnerable moats are weakened or barely intact. The restructuring — 17% workforce cut and Mailchimp pullback — plus GenOS agent monetisation is management's bet that QuickBooks' data flywheel can carry the business even as the TurboTax/Mailchimp bundle shrinks.

analysisPoints.title: QuickBooks: The Fortress Holds (58% of Revenue)
analysisPoints.text: 7M+ SMBs use QuickBooks as their system of record for payroll, invoicing, taxes, and lending. Global Business Solutions Online Ecosystem grew +19% in Q3 FY2026 (+22% ex-Mailchimp), and the segment growth guide was raised to ~16% for FY2026. GenOS agents (Payroll, Project Management in beta; Business Tax Agent) are shipping done-for-you workflows on that data — early claims include faster payment collection and higher deduction capture — while AI-native challengers (Puzzle, Digits) remain subscale.

analysisPoints.title: TurboTax / Credit Karma: Seasonality and Free-Alternative Pressure (Consumer ~24%+)
analysisPoints.text: TurboTax revenue grew just +7% in Q3 FY2026 ($4.4B) — the weakest growth in the portfolio — while Credit Karma printed +15% ($631M) against a full-year CK guide of ~+19% as personal-loan demand normalises. IRS Direct File's elimination removed the biggest government competitor, but FreeTaxUSA and Wealthsimple Tax still chip the paid tier. TurboTax Live (human-assisted, higher ARPU) plus GenOS filing agents (returns completed ~12% faster in early cohorts) are the offsets heading into Investor Day (Sep 17).

analysisPoints.title: Mailchimp Pullback Weakens the Bundle Thesis
analysisPoints.text: The 17% workforce reduction explicitly targets Mailchimp right-sizing and TurboTax/Credit Karma integration redundancy. Management is conceding that the four-product bundle isn't delivering synergies worth the prior cost structure. The bundling moat stays weakened — Intuit is becoming a QuickBooks-centric GenOS platform with supporting consumer products, not a true four-way platform bundle.

growth.description: Latest reported quarter remains Q3 FY2026 (ended Apr 30): revenue $8.56B (+10% YoY) slightly missed consensus, while GAAP EPS $11.09 and non-GAAP EPS $12.80 both beat. FY2026 guidance stands at $21.34–21.37B revenue (+13–14%) and $23.80–$23.85 non-GAAP EPS (+18%); GBS guide ~+16%, Consumer ~+10% (TurboTax ~+7%, Credit Karma ~+19%). The 17% workforce cut ($300–340M charges) is the margin bridge into FY2027. GenOS agentic experiences are live with early engagement metrics, but Q4/FY results (Aug 25 AMC) are not yet reported — do not treat agent KPIs as a substitute for the print.

growthAnalysis.cagrBasis: Measured on company revenue: FY26 guide +13–14% YoY ($21.34–21.37B) after Q3 +10% YoY, with GBS Online +19% YoY (ex-Mailchimp +22% YoY) carrying the stack while TurboTax runs ~+7% YoY and Credit Karma decelerated from +23% YoY (Q2) to +15% YoY (Q3) against a +19% YoY FY CK guide. The 10–13% blended 3–5yr band decays that mix toward mid-teens GBS + mid/high-single-digit Consumer as restructuring expands margins — not an extrapolation of GBS alone, and not a FY27 print (unreported).
growthAnalysis.scoreDerivation: Base 75 (10–13% CAGR midpoint 11.5%) − 1.3 trajectory (Credit Karma decelerating; GBS and TurboTax stable) + 4 margin (expanding via 17% workforce restructuring) − 5 moderate risk (AI-native bookkeeping + TurboTax free-alternative pressure) = 73

valuation.description: Trading ~$331 — ~21% below the base case ($420) — after the post-Q3 selloff and partial bounce. At ~15× non-GAAP forward P/E (NTM) and a PEG near 1.0, Intuit still screens cheap vs quality-software peers (~28–32×), though Street's ~$455 mean target is well below the prior $550–600 cluster. Spot sits between bear ($215) and base; the $8B buyback authorisation and dividend growth cushion downside into the Aug 25 FY print.

peAnalysis.summary: At ~15× non-GAAP forward P/E, Intuit still trades at a deep discount to the quality-software sector median (~28–32×) following the Q3 revenue miss and 17% layoff shock. The PEG near 1.0 signals the market is still pricing AI disruption risk that hasn't shown up in QuickBooks (still +19% GBS Online, +22% ex-Mailchimp). Aug 25 results and Sep 17 Investor Day are the next catalysts for whether GenOS agents and restructuring margin expansion re-rate the multiple.

learnedInterfaces.note: TurboTax's guided interview is directly challenged by AI agents that offer conversational, zero-UI tax filing — including Intuit's own GenOS agents, which abstract the UI that created the switching cost. QuickBooks' interface is stickier but copilots are doing the same abstraction there.

businessLogic.note: QuickBooks' per-SMB configuration depth (chart of accounts, payroll rules, tax integrations, custom invoicing) still requires years of accumulated business logic that AI can't replicate from scratch. IRS Direct File's death removes the biggest government-backed alternative. AI startups haven't cracked enterprise-grade bookkeeping lock-in at scale.

publicDataAccess.note: Tax forms, IRS regulations, and accounting standards are public — AI navigates them efficiently, commoditising Intuit's simplification value. The moat is proprietary user data, not public-data navigation.

talentScarcity.note: The 17% workforce cut is itself evidence that AI has reduced the talent moat — Intuit believes it can operate with 3,000 fewer employees. GenOS rebuilds (skills/tools architecture) further lower the barrier that made TurboTax's guided logic hard to replicate.

bundling.note: Mailchimp right-sizing and the TurboTax/Credit Karma integration layoffs signal management conceding the four-product bundle thesis isn't delivering. Intuit is becoming a QuickBooks-centric GenOS company with supporting products rather than a true synergistic platform bundle.

proprietaryData.note: Tax return data, SMB financial records, and credit profiles for 100M+ users — with hundreds of thousands of attributes per SMB/consumer — is the training set behind GenOS agents (Intuit Assist, Deduction Maximiser, Business Tax Agent). AI makes this moat stronger as the data becomes the training advantage.

regulatoryLockIn.note: IRS authorised e-file partner status, state tax agency relationships, payroll tax compliance, and financial institution integrations remain fully intact. IRS Direct File's elimination by DOGE in 2026 actually strengthened this moat by removing the government-built alternative.

networkEffects.note: CPA-client ecosystem: accountants recommend QuickBooks → clients adopt → data improves → product gets stickier. The 7M+ SMB network is self-reinforcing with high cross-product adoption. Credit Karma's 100M+ member base adds a consumer-side network effect for financial product matching.

transactionEmbedding.note: Payroll runs, invoicing, tax filing, expense tracking, B2B payments, and lending are embedded in the daily operations of 7M+ SMBs — removing Intuit requires re-engineering core business processes. GenOS agents deepen that embedding by acting inside the workflow.

systemOfRecord.note: QuickBooks is the system of record for 7M+ small business finances; TurboTax holds the authoritative tax history of tens of millions of households. Migration risk is prohibitive — you'd lose years of financial history, reconciliation records, and audit trails.

tenMoats.verdict: Intuit is a net beneficiary of AI on balance — its proprietary financial dataset (100M+ users' tax returns, SMB financials, credit profiles) becomes the training-data moat as GenOS agents commoditise interface and business-logic advantages. The five AI-resilient moats remain strong, making QuickBooks structurally durable. The chief AI risk is across the vulnerable moats: agentic point-solutions can replicate individual features cheaply, and the 17% layoff + Mailchimp pullback confirms the bundle thesis is weakening. Durability now hinges on whether GenOS monetises the QuickBooks data flywheel faster than free alternatives erode TurboTax and unbundling shrinks the platform premium — Aug 25 results and Sep 17 Investor Day are the next checkpoints.
